text:
Maya: Dropping a lightweight proposal for 'regional lanes' — a small, product-facing roadmap that ties routing policies, multi-region failover, and customer onramp criteria. Draft: https://redwood.internal/drafts/regional-lanes-alpha 

Maya: Core idea: three lanes (soft-affinity, guarded-affinity, strict-residency). Each lane has clear gates, expected operational burden, and default degradation behaviors. Goal: make sales/CE promises measurable.

Ravi: can we align lanes to selling motions? soft-affinity = self-serve Hosted, guarded = sales-assisted hosted w/ regional hints, strict-residency = Dedicated/Private only.

Sam: agree. also add a mandatory evacuation/rollback checklist per lane. last cutover was painful without one.

Lina: +1. Sales needs a 2-slide checklist for each lane: what we commit, what we measure, what we won't cover. keep it simple.

Maya: proposed 3 gating checks for guarded-affinity alpha: 1) perf: p95 latency under 300ms in-region, 2) observability: tracing + request-level audit logs, 3) capacity: documented committed capacity and fallback policy.

Jesse: add a compliance note for strict-residency: some customers need a signed attestation for data residency. that can be an optional gate for full residency.

Ravi: infra ask: we need a tiny policy DSL that supports preferred_region, failover_region, tenant_quota, model_quota. infra can own runtime but product needs to own semantics.

Sam: infra will prototype a minimal DSL. product should own the test harness (canary prompts, latency cohorts).

Maya: prioritization thought: treat strict-residency customers as high-touch -> Dedicated/Private path. Guarded-affinity covers most affinity asks. reduces platform surface area we need to build.

Lina: can we define two milestones: M1 = guarded-affinity alpha (routing primitives + metrics), M2 = residency pilot (enforcement + billing/contract flow)?

Ravi: M1 = 8 weeks seems doable if we form a small cross-functional squad. ops-bot: @ops-bot created task regional-lanes/M1 assigned to Maya,Ravi,Sam.

ops-bot: Task created: https://tasks.internal/regional-lanes/M1 due 8w from 1876543219.

Jesse: I'll build a customer matrix (top-10 affinity asks) and tag which lane they'd fit. sharing by EOD Fri.

Sam: infra implementation note: start with soft signals (route headers + metrics) then incrementally add strict enforcement. avoids mass migrations.

Maya: nice. we should also surface a simple "isolation readiness" score (0-100) per tenant for GTM. 5 checks roll up to a percentage.

Lina: that will help sales show progress. define checks like: enrollment in billing flow, accepted SLA, perf validation, observability enabled, legal attestation (if needed).

Ravi: also include failure-mode playbooks per lane: e.g., primary region down -> fail to failover-region with warning header OR route to lower-cost model with degraded SLO.

Maya: adding a degradation strategy matrix to the PRD.

Sam: action items recap: 
- Jesse: customer matrix (EOD Fri)
- Sam + Ravi: DSL sketch + lane rollback/evacuation playbook (next Tue)
- Lina: 2-slide GTM checklist + readiness score definition (next Wed)
- Maya: consolidate PRD and link repo/PR

Lina: :thumbsup: this feels actionable. please keep GTM language managed so we don't overpromise.

Maya: will do. tagging folks who want to review the PRD: @Ravi @Sam @Lina @Jesse. I'll post the PRD link when ready.

Sam: ping me for pairing on signals and readiness metrics.

Maya: thanks all. any other blockers?

Ravi: none from infra side.

Jesse: none, will share matrix soon.

Maya: OK closing for now, will update thread with PRD link.
